correctness.rationale: Reflective half-domain energy compression has J=2C-I anti-commuting with reflection, hence off-diagonal parity blocks; odd polynomial f=t h paired with even h yields ∫|t||h|² w>0, so the odd-to-even block is injective and zero eigenspace dimension exactly dim(E)-dim(O), counted by binomial parity formula. All other J eigenvalues pair ± and lie strictly inside (-1,1) by polynomial uniqueness on two open halves. On the uniform unit ball at L=2, exact beta moments give B images of t and t*y_j with singular values s0 and s1; transverse O(d-1) orthogonality, s0>s1, their multiplicities, and gamma asymptotics establish complete quadratic spectrum. Independent generalized Gram matrix calculations reproduce dimensions 2..6.
residual_risks: All-degree half-eigenvalue law only with strict positive reflection-invariant measure on bounded open domain; full remaining spectrum and sharp maximizer only uniformly weighted ball at L=2.

originality.rationale: Gerhards–Huang establish polynomial Slepian concentration and asymptotic eigendistribution on d-ball. Their Theorem 2.1 and Appendix B do not state the exact central half-energy multiplicity for arbitrary finite L or the complete d-dimensional L=2 spectrum. Resultary has an analogous parity-multiplicity theorem for hemispherical spherical harmonics but not d-ball polynomials. The parity anti-commutation is general textbook structure, but the nontrivial injectivity and explicit beta-moment spectrum add an object-specific classification.
residual_risks: An earlier general half-space polynomial parity block theorem might imply the multiplicity; role of positive weight guarantees injectivity.
The 2026 follow-up Gerhards–Huang ACHA paper was not read in full; exact low-degree formulas could occur there.
Full noncentral spectra established only L=2 on uniform ball; arbitrary symmetric domains have pairing and central multiplicity only.
